# BioLights PWM Controller — Documentation for LLMs & AI Agents

> BioLights (`https://www.biolights.nl`) is a browser-based configurator for the BioLights 6-channel horticultural LED PWM controller (a product of Ketten, `https://www.ketten.nl`). It designs 24-hour circadian light schedules and synchronizes them to the microcontroller over USB via the Web Serial API.

## 1. What an LLM Can and Cannot Do (Capabilities & Boundaries)

### What you CAN do as an LLM / AI Agent:
- **Generate complete 24-hour light recipes** tailored to a user's crop, growth stage, and photobiological goals.
- **Give the user a single-line `PROFILE|...` command** that they can copy-paste directly into the **Raw command** box at the bottom of the Communication Terminal on `https://www.biolights.nl` and press **Send** (or `Enter`).
- **Give the user a clickable Deep Link (`https://www.biolights.nl/#profile=...`)** or a **JSON block** that immediately loads your suggested schedule into the visual Spectrum Editor and Setpoint Matrix.

### What you CANNOT do (Human-in-the-Loop Hardware Security):
- **You cannot flash firmware remotely.** To install or update firmware, the user must click **Download .uf2** (`https://www.biolights.nl/pwm_controller.uf2`) and copy the file onto the controller's USB mass-storage drive (BOOTSEL mode) themselves.
- **You cannot connect to USB or write to the hardware automatically.** Pasting a `PROFILE|...` command, opening a Deep Link (`#profile=...`), or pasting JSON **only loads the suggestion into the web preview** (even when no hardware is connected). The user must review the schedule, click **Connect via Serial** (in Chrome, Edge, or Opera), and explicitly click **Sync Time & Setpoints** to upload the schedule to the hardware flash.

---

## 2. Primary Method: Single-Line `PROFILE|...` Command (Copy-Paste into "Raw command")

At the bottom of the **Communication Terminal** on `https://www.biolights.nl`, there is a text input (`Raw command`) with a **Send** button.
When a user asks you for a light schedule, **always give them a single-line `PROFILE|...` command** in a code block so they can copy-paste it into the `Raw command` box and click **Send**:

### Syntax
```text
PROFILE|<sp1>|<sp2>|<sp3>|<sp4>|<sp5>|<sp6>|LABELS,<ch1>,<ch2>,<ch3>,<ch4>,<ch5>,<ch6>|CROP,<crop_name>|NOTE,<short_note>
```

### Rules for the `PROFILE|...` Command:
1. **6 Setpoints (`<sp1>` .. `<sp6>`)**:
   - Format per setpoint: `HH:MM,v1,v2,v3,v4,v5,v6`
   - `HH:MM` is 24-hour time (`00:00` to `23:59`). *(Note: integer minutes since midnight `0..1439` are also accepted, so native `SYNC|<mins>|360,0,0,0,0,0,0|...` lines also work as preview commands!)*
   - `v1..v6` are **6 integer percentages (`0` to `100`)** representing PWM duty cycle for channels `GPIO1` through `GPIO6`.
2. **6 Channel Labels (`LABELS,<ch1>,...,<ch6>`)**:
   - Default hardware channels: `LABELS,UV,Deep Blue,Blue,White,Hyper Red,IR`
   - Colour keywords (`UV`, `Deep Blue`, `Blue`, `White`, `Hyper Red`, `IR`, `Red`, `Green`, `Yellow`, `Orange`, `Purple`, `Cyan`) or numeric wavelengths in nm (e.g. `450`, `660`, `730`) automatically colour the chart lines.
3. **Optional Metadata (`|CROP,...|NOTE,...`)**:
   - Logged in the Communication Terminal alongside any photobiological safety notices when the user clicks **Send**.

### Ready-to-Paste Example (Romaine Lettuce Transplants, 16h Photoperiod):
```text
PROFILE|06:00,0,0,0,0,0,0|07:30,0,30,40,50,45,5|10:00,5,45,55,75,70,10|17:00,5,45,55,75,70,10|20:30,0,20,25,40,50,15|22:00,0,0,0,0,0,0|LABELS,UV,Deep Blue,Blue,White,Hyper Red,IR|CROP,Romaine lettuce transplants|NOTE,16h photoperiod (06:00-22:00), compact morphology, low UV/IR
```

*(Tip: A user can also type `EXPORT` into the Raw command box to print their current table as a `PROFILE|...` one-liner in the terminal, or `HELP` to see the syntax.)*

---

## 3. Hardware & Data Model (6 Channels × 6 Setpoints)

1. **6 PWM Channels (`GPIO1` – `GPIO6`)**:
   - `GPIO1` — **UV** (~385–395 nm UVA)
   - `GPIO2` — **Deep Blue** (~450 nm, chlorophyll b / cryptochrome peak)
   - `GPIO3` — **Blue** (~465–470 nm, stomatal opening / phototropism / compact morphology)
   - `GPIO4` — **White** (broad full-spectrum PAR, ~400–700 nm, visual inspection & canopy penetration)
   - `GPIO5` — **Hyper Red** (~660 nm, primary photosynthesis / chlorophyll a / phytochrome Pr→Pfr)
   - `GPIO6` — **IR** (~730 nm Far-Red, Emerson enhancement effect, shade-avoidance / stem elongation, EOD-FR)

2. **24-Hour Linear Interpolation with Midnight Wrap-Around**:
   - The controller sorts the 6 setpoints chronologically and **linearly interpolates** every channel between adjacent setpoints (including wrapping across midnight between the last setpoint of the day and the first setpoint of the next day).
   - **To keep lights at 0% during the night**, bracket the photoperiod with two `0%` (or night-level) setpoints:
     - Setpoint 1: Sunrise start (e.g. `06:00,0,0,0,0,0,0`) — stays at 0% from Sunset end through the night until 06:00.
     - Setpoint 2: Morning ramp / early phase (e.g. `07:30,...`)
     - Setpoint 3: Midday / main photoperiod start (e.g. `10:00,...`)
     - Setpoint 4: Main photoperiod end / afternoon (e.g. `17:00,...`)
     - Setpoint 5: Evening / End-of-Day treatment (e.g. `20:30,...`)
     - Setpoint 6: Sunset end / night start (e.g. `22:00,0,0,0,0,0,0`) — ramps down to 0% at 22:00 and remains at 0% until Setpoint 1 (`06:00`).

---

## 4. Alternative Formats: Deep Link (`#profile=...`) & JSON Schema

In addition to pasting into the **Raw command** box, `https://www.biolights.nl` also supports:

### A. Clickable Deep Link (`#profile=...`)
You can pass the `PROFILE|...` string (or URL-encoded / Base64 JSON) directly in the URL hash:
`https://www.biolights.nl/#profile=PROFILE|06:00,0,0,0,0,0,0|07:30,0,30,40,50,45,5|10:00,5,45,55,75,70,10|17:00,5,45,55,75,70,10|20:30,0,20,25,40,50,15|22:00,0,0,0,0,0,0|LABELS,UV,Deep%20Blue,Blue,White,Hyper%20Red,IR`

### B. JSON Format (for `Load` button, Drag & Drop, or `Ctrl+V` anywhere on the page)
- Formal JSON Schema: `https://www.biolights.nl/schema/profile-v1.json`
- Default example config: `https://www.biolights.nl/biolights_default_config.json`

```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "metadata": {
    "crop": "Romaine lettuce (transplants / young vegetative)",
    "growth_phase": "Early Vegetative",
    "target_dli": 14,
    "photoperiod_hours": 16,
    "author": "AI Assistant",
    "notes": "16h photoperiod (06:00-22:00). Higher Blue:Red ratio for compact leaf morphology, zero UV/IR stress on young leaves."
  },
  "labels": ["UV", "Deep Blue", "Blue", "White", "Hyper Red", "IR"],
  "setpoints": [
    { "time": "06:00", "values": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] },
    { "time": "07:30", "values": [0, 30, 40, 50, 45, 5] },
    { "time": "10:00", "values": [5, 45, 55, 75, 70, 10] },
    { "time": "17:00", "values": [5, 45, 55, 75, 70, 10] },
    { "time": "20:30", "values": [0, 20, 25, 40, 50, 15] },
    { "time": "22:00", "values": [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5. Photobiological Guidelines for LLM Recipe Generation

- **Seedlings / Rooting / Microgreens**:
  - Moderate intensity (30–55% peak on White/Blue/Hyper Red), 16–18h photoperiod.
  - Keep **UV** low (`0–5%`) and **IR (Far-Red)** low (`0–5%`) to prevent hypocotyl elongation (stretching/etiolation).
- **Vegetative Leafy Greens & Herbs (Lettuce, Basil, Spinach)**:
  - 14–18h photoperiod. Balanced Blue + White + Hyper Red (`50–85%` peak).
  - Moderate UV (`0–15%` mid-day) can stimulate secondary metabolites (anthocyanins, phenolics, essential oils) and leaf thickness.
- **Flowering / Fruiting Crops**:
  - High **Hyper Red (660 nm)** (`70–100%`) and **White** (`70–90%`), supplemented with **IR (730 nm)** (`15–35%`) for Emerson enhancement of photosynthetic efficiency.
- **Sunrise / Sunset & Slew Rate**:
  - Ramp channels gradually over `30–90 minutes` at dawn and dusk rather than jumping from `0%` to `100%` in under 10 minutes (avoids both plant photo-oxidative shock and LED thermal shock).
- **UV Safety**:
  - Avoid sustained UV (`GPIO1`) above `35%` unless specifically requested for short mid-day hormetic UV treatments.
